standard.title: Investigate media arts concepts across contexts
standard.description: investigate the ways that media arts concepts are used in media arts works and practices across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify how media arts concepts are used in works (AC9AMA6E01). They have not yet investigated how cultural, historical and institutional contexts shape how media arts concepts construct representations and position audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how media arts concepts construct representations and position audiences across cultures, times and contexts.

nodes.label: Analysing media arts concepts in works
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and analyse how media arts concepts — cinematography, mise-en-scène, editing, sound — are used to construct representations
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two media arts concepts in a given work; explain how each constructs a representation of a person, place, event or idea
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how media arts concepts are used across a range of works; explain how technical and symbolic codes construct representations and what meanings they produce
wider: Analyse how media languages are used to construct stereotypical representations in media products aimed at teenagers — evaluate how technical codes naturalise those stereotypes
Use Viewpoints questions to analyse cinematography, editing or sound — 'How does this element construct meaning?', 'What ideological position does this representation take?'
Compare how the same media arts concept (e.g. low-angle framing) is used across different genres and evaluate how context changes the meaning produced

response_modes.reason: Students need to build a repertoire of media arts concept examples across multiple works before they can reason about how context shapes representational choices. A single work gives too narrow a base for genuine comparative analysis of how technical codes construct meaning differently across cultures and contexts.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two media arts concepts in a given work
Explains how each constructs a representation — not just names the concept
Does not confuse describing what a work shows with explaining how it constructs meaning

nodes.label: Investigating ideology and audience positioning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how media arts works position audiences to respond to representations and what ideological positions those representations carry
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate how a given media work positions audiences to respond to a representation; explain which technical or symbolic codes produce that positioning
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how audiences are positioned across multiple media works; investigate the ideological or philosophical viewpoints constructed; explain how institutional contexts shape those positions
wider: Investigate the ideology of a media work including what institutions were involved in its distribution and its potential audience impact — evaluate how institutional context shapes representational choices
Analyse how depictions of cultural or social groups in Australian film and television construct meaning for diverse audiences — evaluate how representations serve or challenge dominant ideologies
Investigate how technical and symbolic codes are used to challenge as well as perpetuate unequal power relationships — compare examples that challenge vs reinforce

response_modes.reason: Students commonly analyse media texts as if meaning is fixed in the text, without reasoning about how different audiences in different contexts receive representations differently. Investigating works across cultures, times and institutional contexts — including how the same codes position different audiences differently — forces students to develop audience positioning as an analytical concept rather than assuming universal reception.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The institutional context direction — investigating who distributed the work and what interests shaped its representational choices — opens genuinely rich critical media literacy territory. Advancing students who investigate this develop an understanding of media as an institutional practice, not just an artistic one, which connects to broader critical thinking about how media constructs reality.
success_criteria: Explains how a work positions audiences to respond to a representation
Identifies which technical or symbolic codes produce the positioning
Connects representational choices to ideological position or institutional context

nodes.label: Connecting investigation to own production practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use investigation of how media arts concepts construct representations to inform deliberate choices in own media arts production
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one insight from investigating other works that has influenced a specific decision in own production; explain the connection
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how investigating media arts concepts in existing works informs own choices about technical codes, representations and audience positioning; document specific influences and adaptations
wider: Develop analysis that connects how media arts concepts are used in investigated works to specific production decisions — document the chain from analysis to practice
Investigate how media conventions from another cultural context (e.g. cartooning in Asia) can inform own practice — develop understanding of both influence and cultural appropriation
Construct an argument about why critical investigation of media works produces more deliberate and effective production choices than making without analytical grounding

response_modes.reason: This node requires students to connect concept analysis (Node 1) and ideological investigation (Node 2) to own production decisions. Students who can analyse other works analytically but cannot use that analysis to inform deliberate production choices have not met the standard's full investigative demand.

Students commonly describe what they found in analysed works without articulating how it changes specific production decisions. Scaffolding the connection — what did I learn about how this concept works, what decision does that change in my own work, how is my adaptation different from copying — builds the analytical-to-practical transfer.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one analytical insight that influenced a production decision
Explains the connection between analysis and decision
Distinguishes informed production choice from uncritical imitation
